chunks: Ali, from his brother, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, from Muhammad ibn Talha, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Trimming the moustache and the nails, and washing the head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday negates poverty and increases livelihood.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended grooming practices on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual and material rewards of *al-Ghisl al-Kubra* (major ablution) and grooming on Fridays, specifically highlighting the use of hibiscus (*khitammi*) for its cooling and purifying properties. Scholars interpret the removal of poverty not merely as financial gain but as the alleviation of spiritual neglect, linking physical cleanliness to divine favor and increased sustenance (*rizq*).

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his brother, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq, from Muhammad Bin Talha, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Taking (trimming) the moustache and the nails, and washing the head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday negates the poverty and increases in the livelihood’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his brother from ’Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd al-Khaliq from Muhammad ibn Talhah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Trimming one’s mustache, fingernails and applying al- Khatmi (officinal or marshmallow) to one’s head on Friday removes one’s poverty and increases one’s sustenance.’”
